socrata_assets.name: Child Care Financial Assistance Caseload
socrata_assets.description: The Massachusetts Department of Early Education and Care (EEC) supports access to child care and out-of-school time programs by providing Child Care Financial Assistance (CCFA) to eligible families. This dataset includes the number of unique children served by EEC's CCFA program by month, based on CCFA billing data. The data include disaggregations by age group, region, funding source, agreement type, and provider type. Note that children can be served across multiple categories, but all totals are deduplicated and represent a count of unique children. Therefore, instead of summing across categories, users should use the filters to select specific disaggregations. The billing data for a given month may be updated as additional providers submit their billing information. Categories with fewer than 10 children billed are not included. This dataset is part of EEC's Key Performance Indicator (KPI) Dashboard.

socrata_assets.name: Children Enrolled in Formal Early Education and Care Statewide
socrata_assets.description: This dataset includes the estimated number of children statewide and by region using data from the US Census, as well as the subset of children estimated to be enrolled in formal early education and care programs across the mixed delivery system. Additionally, the dataset includes the total number of children in families with household income below 50% of the state median income and whether all adults in the household are in the labor force, based on data from the US Census, along with the number of children who receive Child Care Financial Assistance (CCFA). This dataset comes from the Child Universal Success Platform (CUSP), an integrated data system developed by Third Sector Intelligence (3Si) in partnership with the Department of Early Education and Care (EEC). CUSP models the full child population in the Commonwealth and estimates the extent to which families are participating in the formal early education and care system. CUSP creates a child population base, drawing on data from the US Census, and uses aggregate capacity data from EEC's Licensing Education Analytic Database (LEAD), aggregate enrollment data from programs participating in Commonwealth Cares for Children (C3), as well as aggregate pre-K enrollment data for district public schools and private schools to estimate the proportion of children served by formal early education and care programs across the mixed delivery system. In this dataset, "formal early education and care" includes enrollment in EEC licensed and funded center based care, family child care programs, district public preschools, and private pre-K programs, but does not include public/private K-12 enrollment or district run afterschool programs. This dataset is part of EEC's Key Performance Indicator (KPI) Dashboard.

socrata_assets.name: Current Licensed and Funded Early Education and Care Programs
socrata_assets.description:
This dataset includes a snapshot of programs currently licensed or funded by the Department of Early Education and Care (EEC). The data is pulled from EEC's Licensing Education Analytic Database (LEAD). For a list of all current and historical early education and care programs please visit the Licensed and Funded Early Education and Care Programs dataset. Data are updated monthly at the beginning of each month.

Licensed programs are programs that are subject to licensing regulations by EEC, which include meeting health and safety standards, training and professional development requirements, criminal and background checks, and maintaining appropriate ratios of educators to children. Licensed programs can include any of the following: family child care and group and school age programs. For more information on licensed programs click here.

Funded programs are programs that are not subject to licensure by EEC but have the approval from EEC to provide subsidized child care for low-income or at-risk families. Funded programs can include any of the following: public schools; private schools; religious schools; and government, tribal, and military child care programs. For more information on funded providers click here.

The types of programs in this dataset include:

  • Licensed Family Child Care is child care provided in someone's home where the caretaker is not related to the children.

  • Licensed Center-Based Care, sometimes called group and school age programs, provide early education and care for young children in a non-residential setting such as a school or community center. These programs include several types of early education and care such as: Center-based care for infants, toddlers, preschool, or kindergarten age children; Early Head Start and Head Start programs; and Out-of- school time programs that operate before/after school or during the summer.

  • Funded Public Schools that participate in CCFA are included here and public schools that do not participate in CCFA are not included here. For data on all public schools with pre-K enrollment, please see the Pre-Kindergarten and Kindergarten Enrollment dataset.

  • Funded Private Schools that participate in CCFA are included here and private schools that do not participate in CCFA are not included here. For data on all private schools with pre-K enrollment, please see the Non-Public School Enrollment dataset.

It provides results by jurisdiction (nation, state, Trial Urban Districts, Puerto Rico, the District of Columbia, and Department of Defense schools) for all main subject areas assessed, including mathematics, reading, writing, and science.

The tool can be used to view tables, run statistical tests, and create charts or other materials that can be exported, saved, copied, and shared with others.

Also known as The Nation’s Report Card, NAEP provides important information about student academic achievement and learning experiences in various subjects. NAEP does not provide scores for individual students or schools; instead, it offers results for populations of students (e.g., fourth-graders) and subgroups of those populations (e.g., female students, Hispanic students) as well as results regarding subject-matter achievement, instructional experiences, and school environment. NAEP results are based on school and student samples that are carefully designed to accurately represent student populations of interest.

socrata_assets.description:

Massachusetts administers the ACCESS for ELLs test annually to all English learners in publicly funded K-12 schools, as required by state and federal law. There are four elements included in this dataset:
  • Reporting Element 1: The number and percent of ELs who make progress towards English language proficiency
  • Reporting Element 2: The number and percent of ELs who attain an ACCESS score indicating English language proficiency
  • Reporting Element 3: The number and percentage of ELs who exit English learner classification based on their attainment of English language proficiency
  • Reporting Element 5: The number and percentage of ELs who have not attained English proficiency within six years of initial classification as an English learner
Reporting Element 4 (the number and percentage of former ELs who have met challenging state academic standards for each of the four years after exiting EL status) is not included in this dataset. For more information about the test administration and reporting elements, please see the WIDA ACCESS page on the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education's website. socrata_assets.name: Special Education Circuit Breaker Reimbursements
socrata_assets.description:
This dataset includes reimbursement amounts provided to Massachusetts public school districts through the Commonwealth's Special Education Circuit Breaker program ("circuit breaker") starting with fiscal year 2006. It also includes expenditure amounts reported to the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) on annual circuit breaker claims. Circuit breaker program reimburses districts for qualified high-cost special education expenditures in two categories: instruction/tuition and transportation. Instruction/tuition has been reimbursed since the program’s inception. Transportation reimbursement was added with the Student Opportunity Act (beginning fiscal year 2022). Districts report costs annually through a claiming process. Expenses over the annual per-student claim threshold are reimbursed quarterly, in the following fiscal year, and at a consistent percentage statewide dependent on available budget. Per statute (M.G.L. Chapter 71B Section 5A), reimbursements are calculated first in the instruction/tuition category. Then, any money left in the state circuit breaker budget line is calculated for transportation reimbursement. Additionally, each year the per-student claim threshold increases based on inflation according to a defined formula. Circuit breaker reimburses through multiple program components:
  • Quarterly payments are provided four times per year and are reimbursements for expenses incurred in the prior fiscal year. Expenses in the instruction and tuition category have been reimbursed since the program's inception. Beginning with the implementation of the Student Opportunity Act (FY22 payments), expenses for out-of-district transportation are also reimbursed.
  • Extraordinary Relief payments are provided once a year to districts showing a significant (greater than 25%) increase in instruction and tuition expenses over the prior year. This reimbursement is provided to qualified districts in the same fiscal year expenses were incurred.
  • Additional/Supplemental payments are provided in atypical scenarios, such as in years when the legislature enacts additional circuit breaker reimbursement mechanisms or authorizes supplemental funding for distribution.
More information regarding the circuit breaker program can be found on the DESE circuit breaker website, including historic information of claim thresholds and percentage reimbursement rates. In addition to the standard reimbursement percentages indicated in the chart, students claimed with special indicators (homeless, state ward or abandoned) are reimbursed at 100% over the claim threshold.

socrata_assets.name: Crosswalk of Career Technical Education (CTE) Programs to Occupations
socrata_assets.description:
This crosswalk maps Massachusetts' Career Technical Education (CTE) pathway programs to aligned occupations. These are defined as occupations that enrolled students are typically prepared to enter upon graduation given the skills and knowledge covered in the program, without any subsequent schooling. The crosswalk was created jointly by the Department of Economic Research (DER) at the Executive Office of Labor and Workforce Development (EOLWD) and the Office of College, Career, and Technical Education at the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE). It matches active CTE program codes found in the Student Information Management System (SIMS) Data Handbook Appendices with occupations in the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) system. Mappings were determined based on standard curriculum described in the CTE Instructional Frameworks as well as occupational requirements observed in recent labor market data. Please note that not all program codes in the SIMS Data Handbook are represented; programs were excluded if no aligned entry-level occupation could be identified, if no graduates had been produced, or if no active programs existed in the state at the time the crosswalk was created. Additional versions of this crosswalk will be created as program curriculum or the labor market changes, when there are changes to the SIMS or SOC coding systems, or as currently excluded programs produce graduates, establish active programs, and develop occupational alignments. Data used to create this crosswalk:
  • SIMS Data Handbook Appendices v1.1 (2025-2026 school year)
  • CTE Instructional Frameworks as of March 2026
  • 2018 SOC system from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (detailed 6-digit codes used, except in cases where labor market information was published in 2023 for aggregated codes)
  • Labor market data from the American Community Survey 5-year (2018-2023) and Lightcast job postings (2025)
For more information on the SOC system or how to use labor market information, please contact economicresearch@mass.gov.

Credits are counted in this dataset if they are submitted to DHE. The credits are counted based on where they are taken, even if that is an institution of higher ed (IHE) outside of the student's designated Early College partnership. Credits from Fall and Spring semester are counted; summer credits are not counted. Data includes any credits at public IHEs (Wentworth Institute of Technology data have not been submitted as of July 2024), and '22-23 data from private IHEs that are part of an Early College designated partnership. The dataset is updated in the fall of each year to add in the previous year's credits. Credit counts are suppressed (hidden) for groups in which there are fewer than 6 students to protect student privacy, though those credits are still counted in totals. The data here are the same as the credit data in the MA Early College Dashboard.

2025 Update on DESE Data on Employment and Earnings  The data link between high school graduates and future earnings makes it possible to follow students beyond high school and college into the workforce, enabling long-term evaluation of educational programs using workforce outcomes. While DESE has published these data in the past, as of June 2025 we are temporarily pausing updates due to an issue conducting the link that was brought to our attention in 2023 by a team of researchers. The issue impacts the earnings information for students who never attended a postsecondary institution or who only attended private or out-of-state colleges or universities, beginning with the 2017 high school graduation cohort, with growing impact in each successive high school graduation cohort. The issue does not impact the earnings information for students who attended a Massachusetts public institution of higher education, and earnings data for those students will continue to be updated. Once a solution is found, the past cohorts of data with low match rates will be updated. DESE and partner agencies are exploring linking strategies to maximize the utility of the information. socrata_assets.description:
The Massachusetts Educator License Mapping Tool links educator licenses to courses. The current version of the mapping tool reflects several important changes from the 2018-19 pilot version, including:
  • Educators with a moderate disabilities and/or severe disabilities license are considered "in-field" for all courses within the grade span and content areas for the license. (e.g. a teacher with a PreK-8 Moderate Disabilities license will be "in-field" when teaching a grade 5 math course but is considered "out-of-field" if teaching grade 4 music).
  • Legacy licenses are appropriately reflected in the crosswalk.
  • Some specific courses were updated with additional licensure fields deemed appropriate. (e.g. a teacher with a Business license will be "in-field" when teaching a marketing course).
  • Updates to the courses that an Early Childhood or Elementary teacher is "in-field" for teaching (e.g. an Elementary teacher is not "in-field" when teaching Music).
Please note that while the mapping tool can serve as guidance to districts in considering hiring and assignment of individual educators, it does not prohibit a district from assigning an out-of-field educator to a course.

socrata_assets.name: Elementary and Secondary District Expenditures Per Pupil
socrata_assets.description:
This dataset contains per-pupil expenditure data for Massachusetts public school districts from 2009 onward. Per-pupil expenditure data for charter schools can be found in the Massachusetts Charter School Financial Dashboard. Districts report expenditure data via the End of Year Financial Report. Per-pupil expenditures are calculated by dividing a district’s operating expenditures by its average pupil membership. Measures include both in-district expenditures per pupil and total expenditures per pupil. The following data elements are used in these calculations:
  • In-District Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) Average Membership: Average enrollment across the school year for pupils enrolled in district schools.
  • In-District Expenditures: All district operating expenditures for in-district programs.
  • In-District Expenditures Per Pupil: Total in-district expenditures divided by in-district FTE average membership.
  • Total FTE Average Membership: Average enrollment across the school year for students enrolled in district schools as well as publicly funded students enrolled in other placements, including charter schools, special education collaboratives, and private special education schools.
  • Total Expenditures: All district operating expenditures, including both in-district programs and out-of-district placements.
  • Total Expenditures Per Pupil: Total expenditures divided by total FTE average membership.
This dataset contains a subset of the data also published in the School Finance Dashboard. For more information about the dashboard and its corresponding datasets, see the School Finance Dashboard landing page in the E2C Hub. Amendments to district expenditures or FTE counts are included in this dataset, meaning data may be updated over time. Per pupil expenditure data is also published on our DESE Profiles site but may differ slightly due to timing of amendments and rounding: Per Pupil Expenditure

socrata_assets.name: Public Postsecondary Annual Enrollment: Detail
socrata_assets.description: This dataset contains the total annual FTE and unduplicated headcount enrollment for undergraduate and graduate students in credit-bearing courses at public community colleges and state universities in Massachusetts since 2014. Data are disaggregated by fiscal year, segment, institution, and student attributes such as enrollment level, residency, age, race/ethnicity, and gender. This dataset is 1 of 2 datasets that is also published in the interactive Annual Enrollment dashboard on the Department of Higher Education Data Center: 1) Public Postsecondary Annual Enrollment: Detail 2) Public Postsecondary Annual Enrollment: Summary Related datasets: 1) Public Postsecondary Fall Enrollment 2) Public Postsecondary Fall Enrollment by Race and Gender Notes: - Data appear as reported to the Massachusetts Department of Higher Education. - Annual enrollment refers to a 12 month enrollment period over one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30). - Figures published by DHE may differ slightly from figures published by other institutions and organizations due to differences in timing of publication, data definitions, and calculation logic. - Data for the University of Massachusetts are not included due to unique reporting requirements. See Fall Enrollment for HEIRS data on UMass enrollment. -The most common measure of enrollment is headcount of enrolled students. Annual headcount enrollment is unduplicated, meaning any individual student is only counted once per institution and fiscal year, even if they are enrolled in multiple terms. - Enrollment can also be measured as full-time equivalent (FTE) students, a calculation based on the sum of credits carried by all enrolled students. In a fiscal year, 30 undergraduate credits = 1 undergraduate FTE, and 24 graduate credits = 1 graduate FTE at a state university. - For precise calculations and aggregations, use the FTE_RAW column. The FTE column is for display only.

socrata_assets.name: Public Postsecondary Tuition and Fees
